title: Functoriality of the associated sheaf on Proj
statement: Let $S=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}S_n$ be an $\mathbf N$-graded commutative ring, $X=\operatorname{Proj}(S)$ [def-nagata-affine-proj], $S_+=\bigoplus_{n>0}S_n$, and $M,N,L$ be $\mathbf Z$-graded $S$-modules. Write $\widetilde M,\widetilde N,\widetilde L$ for their associated sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf] (1), whose sections on $D_+(f)$ for homogeneous $f$ of positive degree are $M_{(f)},N_{(f)},L_{(f)}$. For every degree-preserving $S$-linear map $\phi:M\to N$ there is a unique morphism of $\mathcal O_X$-modules $\widetilde\phi:\widetilde M\to\widetilde N$ whose map on each such $D_+(f)$ is $x/f^m\mapsto\phi(x)/f^m$. For degree-preserving $\psi:N\to L$, $\widetilde{\psi\circ\phi}=\widetilde\psi\circ\widetilde\phi$, and $\widetilde{\mathrm{id}_M}=\mathrm{id}_{\widetilde M}$. If $\mathfrak p$ is a homogeneous prime of $S$ not containing $S_+$ and $x\in X$ is its point, then under the stalk identifications $(\widetilde M)_x=M_{(\mathfrak p)}$ and $(\widetilde N)_x=N_{(\mathfrak p)}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-proj-graded-module-sheaf-exists] (c), the stalk map $(\widetilde\phi)_x$ is $y/h\mapsto\phi(y)/h$ for homogeneous $h\notin\mathfrak p$ and homogeneous $y$ with $\deg y=\deg h$.

proof.text: Localize phi using Mathlib IsLocalizedModule.map and its map_LocalizedModules fraction formula. The prescribed ranges of alpha and degree preservation yield a chart map by choosing preimages; alpha injectivity proves additivity. Prove localized-ring scalar compatibility by fraction induction. Mathlib basicOpenIsoAway and hscalar give linearity over the entire chart section ring. This construction is the proved private helper tilde_chart_map_exists.

For any standard-open inclusion, use standardOpenProperties to choose g^e = a*f. Represent every localized section by y/f^m, without requiring the numerator to be homogeneous. The two hres formulas and phi.map_smul prove naturality of the chart maps. Index the basis by positive homogeneous pairs rather than choosing one denominator per open. Extend the resulting abelian natural transformation with Mathlib TopCat.Sheaf.restrictHomEquivHom. Its extend_hom_app formula and sheaf section_ext prove scalar linearity on all opens, so it is a sheaf-of-modules morphism.

Choose one constructed map for each degree-preserving phi. For two maps obeying the chart formula, fraction induction and alpha injectivity show equality on every positive homogeneous chart. TopCat.Sheaf.hom_ext on the standard-open basis, followed by faithfulness of toPresheaf, gives equality as module-sheaf morphisms. Apply this uniqueness to the composite (using the two fraction formulas) and to the identity to obtain the stated functor laws.

For every source stalk element v, Mathlib exists_mem_germ_eq_of_isBasis represents v as a germ on a positive homogeneous chart. Represent its alpha-image as z/f^n. The denominator f^n belongs to the prime complement because the chart contains the point. Apply hgerm to the source section and to its image under the chart map. Mathlib stalkFunctor_map_germ_apply and map_LocalizedModules give mu_j(stalkMap(v)) = localized(phi)(mu_i(v)). Substitute the given mu_i(s) = y/h and apply map_LocalizedModules again. This works for any h, including degree zero, without multiplying it by a positive homogeneous element.

lean.note: The three modules are indexed by Fin 3. Associated sheaves and their canonical chart/stalk identifications are the data of gradedModuleSheaf_exists, expressed as injective additive maps into the ordinary localizations with prescribed image, scalar law, restriction formula, and germ formula. The conclusion uniquely characterizes induced maps on charts and gives composition, identity, and the stalk fraction formula.
